docs.title: What is Fusion?
docs.text: Fusion is a CLI TCG game that lives in your terminal. You can collect and trade cards with other players, as well as the server. We encourage bots that can make trades and buy from the server and auctions.

docs.title: Why choose Fusion?
docs.text:
We know there are lots of TCG's out there, but Fusion is the best choice for a tech-y TCG.

Feature Fusion Others Card numbering uint16_t Arbitrary Card naming Based on card number Arbitrary Theme Tech/Computers Other Encourages bots? Yes No Runs... CLI In the web Has cool docs? Yes No

docs.title: Servers
docs.text:
Fusion runs multiple servers on the same ip address, with different ports.

The servers run are:

Name Port Protocol Purpose Note Main Server 23 TCP (Netcat) Allows users to connect to Fusion and play the game Human Readable Format HTTP Server 80 HTTP (TCP) Docs and HTTP API Auth Server 4167 UDP Allows external services (like chat servers) to authenticate JSON Format

Note for auth server: View External Services for details on protocal and format.

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
Fusion cards all have an ID and some have a name. The id's range from 0 to 65535 - the uint16_t limit. Some cards have a name, whilst other's just an id. The name typically corresponds to something relate to the id.

Here are some example cards.

Id Name 0 Stdin 1 Stdout 2 Stderr 3 USB 3.0 4 IPv4 5 Raspberry Pi 5 6 Unix V6 7 Windows 7 8 uint8_t 10 OS-X 16 Base 16 - Hex 21 FTP - Port 21 22 SSH - Port 22 23 Telnet - Port 23 64 Commodore 64 80 HTTP - Port 80 84 TI-84 255 0xFF

docs.title: Currency
docs.text:
Fusion uses a custom currency with multiple different coins.

The coins are:

  • Megons (10 Kilons)
  • Kilons (10 Unons)
  • Unons (10 Milons)
  • Milons (10 Microns)
  • Microns (10 Nanons)
  • Nanons (10 Picons)
  • Picons

Each coin is worth 10 times the previous. I.E. 10 Picons = 1 Nanon, 10 Nanons = 1 Micron, etc.

For comparison, 1 Picon is approximately $0.01 USD and 1 Nanon is $0.10 USD.

NOTE: You CAN NOT buy coins for Fusion with real life money and anyone claiming to sell them is likely trying to scam you.

If you do not seee a unit, then assume it is in unons.

docs.title: token <+|-|list|get|def> [name]
docs.text:
Manage auth tokens.

  • token list — List all saved tokens
  • token + mytoken — Create a new token named "mytoken"
  • token - mytoken — Delete the token named "mytoken"
  • token get mytoken — Print the value of "mytoken"
  • token def mytoken - Sets default token as "mytoken"

docs.title: servers <+|-|list|get> [name]
docs.text:
Manage server aliases.

  • servers list — List all saved servers
  • servers + prod — Add a server aliased "prod"
  • servers - prod — Remove the server aliased "prod"
  • servers get prod — Print the URL for "prod"

docs.title: connect-chat <url|name> [token-name]
docs.text:
Connect to a chat server.

  • connect-chat prod — Connect using saved server alias "prod"
  • connect-chat tcp://localhost:1337 — Connect by URL directly
  • connect-chat prod mytoken — Connect using alias "prod" and token "mytoken"

docs.title: message <message> [@username]
docs.text:
Send a chat message.

  • message hello everyone! — Broadcast to all connected users
  • message hey @alice — Send directly to alice

docs.title: chat-console
docs.text:
Enter interactive chat mode.

  • chat-console — Opens the console — type exit to leave

<required> [optional]

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
You can connect over TCP with Telnet, Netcat or another client.

The server address is localhost:23

docs.title: Connecting with Windows
docs.text:
First, you need to install Telnet. If you already have Telnet installed, you can skip this step.

Open powershell or command prompt and run:

dism /online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:TelnetClient

Then, connect to Fusion:

telnet localhost 23

docs.title: Connecting with Mac
docs.text:
In order to install Telnet, you need a package manager. The standard MacOS package manager is Brew. If you already have Brew installed, you can skip this step (To check, run brew --version).

Open Terminal and run:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

Then to install telnet, run:

brew install telnet

Now, you can connect to Fusion with:

telnet localhost 23

docs.title: Connecting with Linux
docs.text:
In order to install Telnet, you need to install APT, a package manager. You probably already have APT installed.

Note for Chromebook users: You need to install the Linux development environment for the Terminal app to work.

To check, run in your Terminal:

apt --version

If the command succeeds, then you can proceed to the next step (Using APT).

Then, install telnet with APT.

apt install telnet

You can now connect to Fusion with:

telnet localhost 23

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
External services allow you to connect Fusion to other things. Some examples include:

  • Chat servers
  • etc.

In order to conenct an external service, you first need to make a token. A token is a large number that can be used to authenticate yourself with these services.

We do not recommend reusing tokens for multiple services because this could lead to security issues.

In order to make a token, you can run the command: token + <name> where <name> is whatever you would like to call the token.

Once you have created a token, you can use it to connect to external services.

docs.title: Auth Server Protocal
docs.text:
The auth server uses a UDP protocal that lets you get a username from a token. You send a UDP packet with the access token as a string, terminated by a new line (\n);

The server will then reply with a username if the token is valid, or ... if not. Both are terminated by a new line.

For example:

Client --> Server:      628efc1596b8fdff931cd9c087defbc8
Server --> Client:      simon

Client2 --> Server:     notarealtoken1234
Server  --> Client2:    ...

docs.title: Chat Server Protocal
docs.text:
The chat server uses a TCP connection sending JSON data. Every request has a type field which identifies the packet type and every response has a success field which indicates if the response succeeded.

A succesful response also had a type field. A failed response has a error field which details the error. Both responses have message field.

Request:

{
    "type": "<type>",
    ...
}

Succesful response:

{
    "success": true,
    "type": "<packet_type",
    "message": "<readable_message>"
}

Failed response:

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "<error_message>",
    "message": "<readable_message>"
}

docs.title: Request types
docs.text: There are three request types: login, message, and quit.

docs.title: login
docs.text:
The login command takes in an accessToken field.

{
    "type": "login",
    "accessToken": "628efc1596b8fdff931cd9c087defbc8"
}

The chat server will then verify with the authentication server.

Success

{
    "success": true,
    "type": "login",
    "message": "Login successful.",
    "username": "simon"
}

Failure

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_MISSING_ACCESS_TOKEN",
    "message": "Missing required field: accessToken."
}

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN",
    "message": "The provided access token is invalid or expired."
}

docs.title: message
docs.text:
Note: You must be logged in to send this command.

The message command takes in a message field and optionally a to field. If no to field is sent, then it is broadcasted to everybody.

{
    "type": "message",
    "message": "Hello, Everyone!",
    [OPTIONALLY] "to": "bob"
}

Success — sent to the sender after the message is delivered

{
    "success": true,
    "type": "message_sent",
    "message": "Message sent."
}

Received — sent to the recipient(s)

{
    "success": true,
    "type": "message",
    "from": "simon",
    "message": "Hello, Everyone!",
    "direct": false
}

The direct field is true if the message was sent to a specific user via the to field, and false if it was broadcast.

Failure

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_NOT_AUTHENTICATED",
    "message": "You must be logged in to send messages."
}

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_MISSING_MESSAGE",
    "message": "Missing required field: message."
}

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "User \"bob\" not found or not online."
}

docs.title: quit
docs.text:
Disconnects from the server.

{
    "type": "quit"
}

Success

{
    "success": true,
    "type": "quit",
    "message": "Goodbye."
}

docs.title: General errors
docs.text:
These can be returned for any request.

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_NEEDS_TO_BE_JSON",
    "message": "Request body must be valid JSON."
}

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_MISSING_TYPE",
    "message": "Missing required field: type."
}

{
    "success": false,
    "error": "ERR_UNKNOWN_CMD",
    "message": "Unknown command type: \"<type>\"."
}

docs.title: HTTP Card API
docs.text: The HTTP Card API primarily uses GET and POST requests to the same HTTP server that the docs are running on.

docs.title: GET /api/cards.csv
docs.text: Returns a CSV (Comma Separated Value list) of all the cards.

docs.title: GET /api/seasons.csv
docs.text: Returns a CSV (Comma Separated Value list) of all the seasons.
